import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.45

by V. M. Petechuk

Let $n \geq 3$ and suppose that $N$ is a subgroup of $GL_n(R)$ which is normalized by
$E_n(R)$. Prove that either $N$ contains $E_n(R)$ or $\Lambda_I[N, E_n(R)] = 1$ for a
suitable ideal $I \ne R$ of $R$.

Here $R$ is an arbitrary associative ring with $1$ (not necessarily commutative), $E_n(R)$ is
the elementary subgroup of $GL_n(R)$, i.e. the subgroup generated by the elementary
transvections $t_{ij}(a) = 1 + a e_{ij}$ ($i \ne j$, $a \in R$), ideals are two-sided, and
$\Lambda_I : GL_n(R) \to GL_n(R/I)$ is the reduction homomorphism modulo $I$. Thus
$\Lambda_I[N, E_n(R)] = 1$ means that every element of the commutator subgroup
$[N, E_n(R)]$ is congruent to the identity matrix modulo $I$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.45»

variable (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) [Ring R]

variable {n R} in
/-- The elementary transvection $t_{ij}(a) = 1 + a e_{ij}$, for $i \ne j$ and $a \in R$, as an
element of $GL_n(R)$; its inverse is $t_{ij}(-a) = 1 - a e_{ij}$. -/
def elementaryTransvection {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) (a : R) : GL (Fin n) R where
  val := 1 + Matrix.single i j a
  inv := 1 - Matrix.single i j a
  val_inv := by
    simp [add_mul, mul_sub, Matrix.single_mul_single_of_ne _ _ _ _ hij.symm]
  inv_val := by
    simp [sub_mul, mul_add, Matrix.single_mul_single_of_ne _ _ _ _ hij.symm]

/-- The elementary subgroup $E_n(R)$ of $GL_n(R)$: the subgroup generated by all elementary
transvections $t_{ij}(a)$ with $i \ne j$ and $a \in R$. -/
def elementarySubgroup : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) R) :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) (a : R), g = elementaryTransvection hij a}

/-- The reduction homomorphism $\Lambda_I : GL_n(R) \to GL_n(R/I)$ modulo a two-sided ideal
$I$ of $R$, induced by the quotient map $R \to R/I$ applied entrywise. -/
def reductionHom (I : Ideal R) [I.IsTwoSided] : GL (Fin n) R →* GL (Fin n) (R ⧸ I) :=
  Units.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I).mapMatrix.toMonoidHom

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem elementaryTransvection_zero {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    elementaryTransvection hij (0 : R) = 1 := by
  ext
  simp [elementaryTransvection]

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem elementaryTransvection_mem_elementarySubgroup {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) (a : R) :
    elementaryTransvection hij a ∈ elementarySubgroup n R :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨i, j, hij, a, rfl⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem coe_reductionHom_apply (I : Ideal R) [I.IsTwoSided] (g : GL (Fin n) R) (i j : Fin n) :
    (reductionHom n R I g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (R ⧸ I)) i j = Ideal.Quotient.mk I (g i j) :=
  rfl

/--
Let $R$ be an associative ring with $1$, let $n \geq 3$ and suppose that $N$ is a subgroup of
$GL_n(R)$ which is normalized by $E_n(R)$. Then either $N$ contains $E_n(R)$, or there is a
two-sided ideal $I \ne R$ of $R$ such that $\Lambda_I[N, E_n(R)] = 1$, i.e. the image of the
commutator subgroup $[N, E_n(R)]$ under the reduction homomorphism
$\Lambda_I : GL_n(R) \to GL_n(R/I)$ is trivial.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.45» (hn : 3 ≤ n) (N : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) R))
    (hN : elementarySubgroup n R ≤ N.normalizer) :
    elementarySubgroup n R ≤ N ∨
      ∃ (I : Ideal R) (_ : I.IsTwoSided), I ≠ ⊤ ∧
        Subgroup.map (reductionHom n R I) ⁅N, elementarySubgroup n R⁆ = ⊥ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.45»

by V. M. Petechuk

elementary subgroup $E_n(R)$. Must either $N$ contain $E_n(R)$, or the
commutator subgroup $[N,E_n(R)]$ be trivial modulo some proper two-sided ideal
of $R$?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.45»

/-- The elementary transvection $1 + cE_{ij}$, regarded as an invertible
matrix over an associative unital ring. -/
def elementaryTransvectionUnit {R : Type*} [Ring R] {n : ℕ}
    (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) (c : R) : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) R where
  val := 1 + Matrix.single i j c
  inv := 1 + Matrix.single i j (-c)
  val_inv := by
    simp only [Matrix.add_mul, Matrix.mul_add, Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.mul_one]
    rw [Matrix.single_mul_single_of_ne c i j i hij.symm (-c)]
    simp only [add_zero]
    rw [add_assoc, ← Matrix.single_add]
    simp
  inv_val := by
    simp only [Matrix.add_mul, Matrix.mul_add, Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.mul_one]
    rw [Matrix.single_mul_single_of_ne (-c) i j i hij.symm c]
    simp only [add_zero]
    rw [add_assoc, ← Matrix.single_add]
    simp

/-- The elementary subgroup $E_n(R)$ of $GL_n(R)$, generated by all elementary
transvections $1 + cE_{ij}$ with $i \ne j$. -/
def elementaryGroup (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) [Ring R] :
    Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) R) :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) (c : R),
    g = elementaryTransvectionUnit i j hij c}

/-- The homomorphism on general linear groups obtained by applying a ring
homomorphism entrywise. -/
def generalLinearMap {R S : Type*} [Ring R] [Ring S] {n : ℕ} (f : R →+* S) :
    Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) R →* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) S :=
  Units.map (RingHom.mapMatrix f).toMonoidHom

/-- Reduction modulo a two-sided ideal, as a homomorphism from $GL_n(R)$ to
$GL_n(R/I)$. -/
def reductionMap {R : Type*} [Ring R] {n : ℕ} (I : TwoSidedIdeal R) :
    Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) R →*
      Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) I.ringCon.Quotient :=
  generalLinearMap I.ringCon.mk'

/--
Let $n \geq 3$ and suppose that $N \leq GL_n(R)$ is normalized by $E_n(R)$.
Then either $N$ contains $E_n(R)$, or there is a proper two-sided ideal
$I \ne R$ such that the reduction map $\Lambda_I$ sends the commutator subgroup
$[N,E_n(R)]$ to the trivial subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.45» :
    ∀ (R : Type*) [Ring R] (n : ℕ) (_ : 3 ≤ n)
      (N : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) R)),
      elementaryGroup n R ≤ N.normalizer →
        elementaryGroup n R ≤ N ∨
          ∃ I : TwoSidedIdeal R, I ≠ ⊤ ∧
            ⁅N, elementaryGroup n R⁆ ≤ (reductionMap I).ker := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.45»

The matrix size n is represented by the index type `Fin n`, and the source condition n ≥ 3 is stated as `3 ≤ n`.
The elementary subgroup E_n(R) is the subgroup closure of all units represented by matrices `1 + Matrix.single i j c` with `i ≠ j` and `c : R`.
“N is normalized by E_n(R)” is represented as `elementaryGroup n R ≤ N.normalizer`.
An ideal of a possibly noncommutative ring is represented by `TwoSidedIdeal R`; `I ≠ R` is represented by `I ≠ ⊤`.
The reduction map Λ_I applies the quotient ring homomorphism entrywise to invertible matrices.
The equation Λ_I[N,E_n(R)] = 1 is represented equivalently by inclusion of the subgroup commutator `⁅N, elementaryGroup n R⁆` in the kernel of the reduction homomorphism.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

open Matrix

namespace Kourovka.«10.45»

variable {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Ring R]

/-- The elementary transvection $t_{ij}(c) = 1 + c\,e_{ij}$ (for $i \ne j$) as an element of
$GL_n(R)$. Its inverse is $t_{ij}(-c)$. -/
def elementaryTransvection (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) (c : R) : GL (Fin n) R where
  val := 1 + single i j c
  inv := 1 + single i j (-c)
  val_inv := by
    have h : single i j c * single i j (-c) = 0 := single_mul_single_of_ne _ _ _ _ hij.symm _
    simp [add_mul, mul_add, h, add_assoc, ← single_add]
  inv_val := by
    have h : single i j (-c) * single i j c = 0 := single_mul_single_of_ne _ _ _ _ hij.symm _
    simp [add_mul, mul_add, h, add_assoc, ← single_add]

/-- The elementary subgroup $E_n(R) \le GL_n(R)$, generated by all elementary transvections
$t_{ij}(c)$ with $i \ne j$ and $c \in R$. -/
def elementarySubgroup (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) [Ring R] : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) R) :=
  Subgroup.closure
    {g | ∃ (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) (c : R), g = elementaryTransvection i j hij c}

/-- The reduction homomorphism $\Lambda_I : GL_n(R) \to GL_n(R/I)$ modulo a two-sided ideal
$I$ of $R$, applying the quotient map $R \to R/I$ entrywise. -/
def reductionHom (I : Ideal R) [I.IsTwoSided] : GL (Fin n) R →* GL (Fin n) (R ⧸ I) :=
  Units.map (RingHom.mapMatrix (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).toMonoidHom

theorem coe_elementaryTransvection (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) (c : R) :
    (elementaryTransvection i j hij c : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) = 1 + single i j c :=
  rfl

theorem coe_reductionHom_apply (I : Ideal R) [I.IsTwoSided] (g : GL (Fin n) R) (a b : Fin n) :
    (reductionHom I g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (R ⧸ I)) a b = Ideal.Quotient.mk I (g a b) :=
  rfl

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem elementaryTransvection_mem_elementarySubgroup (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) (c : R) :
    elementaryTransvection i j hij c ∈ elementarySubgroup n R :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨i, j, hij, c, rfl⟩

Let $n \geq 3$ and suppose that $N$ is a subgroup of $GL_n(R)$ which is normalized by
$E_n(R)$. Prove that either $N$ contains $E_n(R)$ or $\Lambda_I[N, E_n(R)] = 1$ for a
suitable ideal $I \ne R$ of $R$.

Here $R$ is an arbitrary associative ring with $1$, $I$ ranges over two-sided ideals of $R$,
and $\Lambda_I : GL_n(R) \to GL_n(R/I)$ is reduction modulo $I$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.45» (hn : 3 ≤ n) (N : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) R))
    (hN : elementarySubgroup n R ≤ N.normalizer) :
    elementarySubgroup n R ≤ N ∨
      ∃ (I : Ideal R) (_ : I.IsTwoSided), I ≠ ⊤ ∧
        (⁅N, elementarySubgroup n R⁆).map (reductionHom I) = ⊥ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.45»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.45

by V. M. Petechuk

Let $n \geq 3$, and let $N$ be a subgroup of $GL_n(R)$ normalized by the
elementary subgroup $E_n(R)$. Then either $N$ contains $E_n(R)$, or the
commutator subgroup $[N,E_n(R)]$ is trivial modulo some proper ideal of $R$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Matrix

namespace Kourovka.«10.45»

variable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
variable {R : Type*} [Ring R]

/-- The elementary transvection $1 + r e_{ij}$, where $i \ne j$, regarded as
an element of $GL_\iota(R)$. -/
def elementaryTransvection (i j : ι) (hij : i ≠ j) (r : R) :
    Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup ι R where
  val := 1 + Matrix.single i j r
  inv := 1 + Matrix.single i j (-r)
  val_inv := by
    simp only [add_mul, mul_add, one_mul]
    rw [Matrix.single_mul_single_of_ne r i j i hij.symm (-r)]
    ext a b
    by_cases h : i = a ∧ j = b <;> simp [h]
  inv_val := by
    simp only [add_mul, mul_add, one_mul]
    rw [Matrix.single_mul_single_of_ne (-r) i j i hij.symm r]
    ext a b
    by_cases h : i = a ∧ j = b <;> simp [h]

/-- The elementary subgroup $E_\iota(R)$ of $GL_\iota(R)$, generated by the
elementary transvections $1 + r e_{ij}$ for $i \ne j$ and $r \in R$. -/
def elementarySubgroup : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup ι R) :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ (i j : ι) (hij : i ≠ j) (r : R),
    elementaryTransvection i j hij r = g}

/--
Let $n \geq 3$, and suppose that $N \leq GL_n(R)$ is normalized by $E_n(R)$.
Then either $E_n(R) \leq N$, or there is a proper two-sided ideal $I$ of $R$
such that $[N,E_n(R)]$ lies in the kernel of the reduction homomorphism
$GL_n(R) \to GL_n(R/I)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.45» :
    ∀ (R : Type) [Ring R] (n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n →
      ∀ N : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) R),
        (elementarySubgroup (ι := Fin n) (R := R)) ≤ N.normalizer →
        (elementarySubgroup (ι := Fin n) (R := R)) ≤ N ∨
          ∃ (I : Ideal R) (_ : I.IsTwoSided), I ≠ ⊤ ∧
            ⁅N, (elementarySubgroup (ι := Fin n) (R := R))⁆ ≤
              (Units.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I).mapMatrix.toMonoidHom).ker := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.45»
modeling_decisions: The unspecified ring is modeled as an arbitrary associative unital `Ring`, without assuming commutativity or nontriviality.
For a noncommutative ring, an ideal suitable for forming `R/I` is modeled as an `Ideal R` equipped with `I.IsTwoSided`; properness is `I ≠ ⊤`.
“N is normalized by E_n(R)” is expressed as `E_n(R) ≤ N.normalizer`.
The notation `Λ_I[N,E_n(R)] = 1` is expressed equivalently as the subgroup commutator lying in the kernel of the homomorphism induced entrywise by `Ideal.Quotient.mk I`.
`E_n(R)` is the subgroup closure of all matrices `1 + r e_{ij}` with `i ≠ j`. Matrix indices are `Fin n`.
